:::{#thm-kronecker-outer-product}
#### An outer product is a Kronecker product

For a vector $\vecf{u}$ with $m$ entries
and a vector $\vecf{v}$ with $n$ entries,
the [Kronecker product](#def-kronecker-product) of the column vector $\vecf{u}$
with the row vector $\tp{\vecf{v}}$
[equals](linear-algebra.qmd#def-matrix-equality) the [outer product](#def-outer-product) $\oprod{\vecf{u}}{\vecf{v}}$:

$$
\underbrace{\vecf{u}}_{m \times 1} \otimes \underbrace{\tp{\vecf{v}}}_{1 \times n}
= \underbrace{\oprod{\vecf{u}}{\vecf{v}}}_{m \times n}
$$

:::

::: proof

The Kronecker product $\vecf{u} \otimes \tp{\vecf{v}}$ has one column of blocks,
and its block in row $i$ is $u_i \tp{\vecf{v}}$, a $1 \times n$ row.
So entry $(i, j)$ of each side, for $i$ from $1$ to $m$ and $j$ from $1$ to $n$, is

$$
\ba
\paren{\vecf{u} \otimes \tp{\vecf{v}}}_{ij}
&= \paren{u_i \tp{\vecf{v}}}_{j}
&& \text{(definition of the Kronecker product)}
\\
&= u_i v_j
&& \text{(entry } j \text{ of the scalar multiple } u_i \tp{\vecf{v}} \text{)}
\\
&= \paren{\oprod{\vecf{u}}{\vecf{v}}}_{ij}
&& \text{(entries of an outer product)}
\ea
$$

:::
